global_silver_linings.title: Good News in History, October 4
global_silver_linings.snippet: 22 years ago today, SpaceShipOne, funded by Microsoft’s Paul Allen, became the first private manned spacecraft to fly into sub-orbital space. That same year, its innovative design won the $10 million Ansari X Prize. Piloted and returned to Earth by Mike Melvill, he became the first-ever licensed US commercial astronaut.
global_silver_linings.reason: History is full of quietly remarkable moments worth remembering, and pausing to reflect on the good that has come before reminds us that progress is real and cumulative. Each October 4th milestone is a thread in a longer story of human resilience and kindness.

global_silver_linings.title: The 13 signs that someone is ‘dangerously good’ at reading people
global_silver_linings.snippet: "You feel comfortable talking to them, and you find yourself sharing things with them that you don’t typically share."
global_silver_linings.reason: Deep empathy and the ability to truly understand others are skills that strengthen relationships and build kinder communities. Recognising and nurturing these traits in ourselves and those around us is a small but meaningful step toward a more connected world.

featured_read.title: Do Calorie‑Restricted Diets Work?
featured_read.snippet: Or will I just re‑gain the weight?
featured_read.blurb: Science keeps promising that eating less will reset your body for good — this piece quietly interrogates why that promise keeps slipping through our fingers. A rigorous, honest look at what calorie restriction actually does (and doesn't do) once the study ends.

reading_room.title: The Top 5 Longreads of the Week
reading_room.snippet: Recommending notable stories from Caitlin Dickerson, Marci Wilding, Tiffany Huang, Nick Paumgarten, and Chabeli Carrazana.
reading_room.blurb: Five writers doing their best work this week, gathered in one place — the kind of list worth bookmarking before the weekend arrives and you suddenly have an hour to yourself.

reading_room.title: 10 Great Nonfiction Titles to Enjoy in October
reading_room.snippet: Next month offers an incredible selection of nonfiction, including work by David Treuer, Wendy S. Walters, Thomas Frank, and more. Shop the List on Bookshop.org * Savage Mind, David Treuer David Treuer is a true triple threat as a writer:
reading_room.blurb: October's nonfiction slate, anchored by David Treuer's singular voice, makes a case that autumn is genuinely the best season to sit down with a book that wants to change your mind about something.

reading_room.title: Eric Schmitt’s Very Bad Day at Work
reading_room.snippet: For MAGA politicians, there’s no such thing as a gaffe.
reading_room.blurb: A close read of one senator's stumble reveals something unsettling about the new rules of political accountability — or the quiet disappearance of them.

reading_room.title: The Best Seller That’s Nearly Impossible to Finish Reading
reading_room.snippet: James Patterson and MrBeast wrote a book in hopes of reaching young people.
reading_room.blurb: Two of the most algorithmically successful humans alive tried to write a book together for teenagers, and the result raises a sharp question: what happens when reach becomes the only measure of worth in storytelling?

reading_room.title: “Floating Scarecrow” Demonstrates the Enduring Power of Eyes in the Natural World
reading_room.blurb: Eyes painted on a buoy are enough to send seabirds veering off course — this essay follows that eerie fact into a deeper reckoning with how profoundly the feeling of being watched shapes behavior across the animal kingdom.

Pull on a layer before you head out; the garden is damp with dew and perfectly, crisply itself.

And what could be more warming and comforting than a spiced vodka and citrus cocktail spiced with nut liqueur? Slice of carrot cake optional.
news.blurb: A spiced cocktail designed to keep company with carrot cake is exactly the sort of autumnal indulgence that makes the season's chill feel like a gift rather than a grievance.

recipe.title: simple chicken tacos
recipe.snippet: Twenty years ago, I started this website because I wanted a place to share recipes I was excited about, as it’s practically coded into my DNA to be an unfettered yap about the things I love. [ This is me. ] The larger context was that upon reaching so-called adulthood, I’d found that while I knew how to cook, there were still so many things I hadn’t figured out, such as: how to turn a can of tomatoes into not just an okay pasta sauce, but a spectacular one ; how to make really good meatballs ; perfect hummus ; and a crumb cake I’d want to make forever.
recipe.blurb: These simple chicken tacos from Smitten Kitchen are the kind of weeknight salvation you'll want in your back pocket — unfussy, satisfying, and the sort of thing that earns a permanent spot in the rotation from the very first bite.

larder.seasonal_note: Zürich's markets are piled with Berner Rosen and Maigold apples right now, and there's no better mid-autumn morning ritual than picking up a bag on your way home from the Helvetiaplatz market, then slow-cooking them into a rough Apfelmus to spoon over your Haferbrei while the city's chestnuts roast somewhere just around the corner.
